item.detail: 14 failed SSH logins in 5 minutes, then a successful login

cases.name: Login after brute-force burst (14 failures, then success)
cases.notes: A success right after a guessing burst means the password was likely guessed.

item.detail: 8 failed SSH logins in 3 minutes, then a successful login

cases.name: Login after brute-force burst (8 failures, then success)
cases.notes: Same pattern, different source — the verdict must not depend on the IP.

item.detail: 12 failed SSH logins in 5 minutes, no success recorded

cases.name: Brute-force burst, no success yet (12 failures)
cases.notes: Guessing is likely, but without a success it cannot be confirmed.

item.detail: 30 failed SSH logins in 10 minutes, no success recorded

cases.name: Brute-force burst, no success yet (30 failures)
cases.notes: A bigger burst is still only likely until a login succeeds.

cases.name: Brute-force burst with missing optional fields
cases.notes: The agent must still triage when count and detail are absent.

cases.name: Open Telnet port on a host
cases.notes: No attack recorded, but cleartext credentials make this worth fixing.

cases.name: Open SSH port on a host
cases.notes: Normal for a server; risk depends on password login and exposure.

cases.name: Open HTTP port on a host
cases.notes: A web service is exposed; patch level decides the real risk.

cases.name: Open RDP port on a host
cases.notes: RDP exposure needs a human to check whether it faces the internet.

item.detail: Wazuh rule 5710 level 12 fired on the web server

cases.name: High-level Wazuh host alert
cases.notes: One alert alone is not enough to confirm a threat; correlate first.

item.detail: A host scanned several ports on the network

cases.name: Incident of an unknown type
cases.notes: Unknown kinds must degrade to review, never to a confident verdict.

cases.name: Open port with an unknown service
cases.notes: No guidance entry exists for this service, so the agent must not guess.
